hypothesis: Early-session rlm.spawn cold-exec outliers (400-990ms recorded in handoffs) persist at the current tip and live in the spawn admission (supervisor-side child worker creation), not in the kernel venv/import phases (which are depth-0-gated out of children and land on the child's FIRST TOOL CALL), and not in the turn/wire path (sub-ms). Post-#2857 the per-worker process-global probe memo misses on every fresh child worker, so each child's first kernel start re-pays the direct probe chain.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change. New daemon-direct probe driver (spawn_probe.py, orchestrator copy at hillclimb/spawn-work/vm-files/): JSONL protocol-7 wire client (bench daemon_boot adapter port) drives a REAL parent session (prime-inference/mock-1 via models.json) on a real supervisor; the offline mock provider (bench mock_provider.py, port 8890) serves parent turns with an ipython toolCall that runs `await rlm.spawn(...)` inside the parent kernel (kernel-side receipt: perf_counter spawn span + admit clocks), child turns with an ipython cell writing a child receipt (child kernel ready). Oracles: PI_REQUEST_TIMING=1 phase rows (agent.jsonl, pid+sessionId), per-request mock arrival log with queue audit, 2ms /proc process grid (worker/probe-python/kernel-python first sightings, classified by cmdline), child session-file row ledger, driver wire spans (accept/hello/create/prompt), per-trial receipts with wall+monotonic clocks (all processes share CLOCK_MONOTONIC), calibration (python loop + loadavg) pre/mid/post per trial. Regimes: cold_daemon x warm venv n=10 (fresh daemon+agent dir per trial, shared venv), warm_daemon shared n=8 (one daemon+parent, warmup cell boots the parent kernel, one spawn per trial turn), warm_daemon x 10MiB parent fixture n=6 (deterministic bench fixture sha dadaecfcac511e24ed0e0df15fb1facbe556557856486d62bad628250194cdda, 7391 rows, resumed via sessionPath), cold_daemon x cold venv n=3 (fresh kernel venv per trial, warm uv cache + seeded uv python). Shared-regime harness note: mock_state matches a request against EVERY user message in history, so prior-prompt markers keep matching; each trial gets its own queue keyed by its own prompt marker, newest first, with [toolCell, text] pairs so turn parity holds through arbitrary child-notice turns; all cells are replay-idempotent (receipt-preserving) and replays write .replay side-receipts. Standalone components on the same VM: RUNTIME_READY_CHECK probe (fresh process) x7, python -c 'import rlm' x7, raw kernel boot (python -m rlm.repl -> protocol-3 ready) x7, plus 4KB fsync probes bracketing the cold-arm rerun.
parity_notes: No product code changed in any phase; frozen parity untouched (spawn semantics/wire/session replay). The probe drives the production path: real parent session, real supervisor create/prompt wire, real child worker processes, real kernel venv bootstrap/probe/python chain. Mock provider is offline-only (bench harness, not part of any product); parent/child model = prime-inference/mock-1 from models.json. Privacy: fixtures are deterministic bench fixtures; records carry sha256/counts only. Tool-name contract: the mock's ipython toolCall exercises the same kernel tool dispatch production uses.

validity.notes: Single-driver discipline: one probe process per regime run, sequential trials, no concurrent probe instances (an early duplicated-driver incident was caught, cleaned, and all affected data discarded; every kept trial comes from the post-cleanup single-driver runs). The shared-daemon regimes accumulate child-notice turns; per-trial queue keys + replay-idempotent cells keep the mock deterministic (queue hits audited per trial: every parent request matched its own trial queue, every child request the child queue, aux hits 0). The 400-990ms cold-exec outliers from the handoffs were NOT reproduced at the healthy window: worst admission 438ms (degraded window) / 338ms (healthy); the handoff 976ms figure was a daemon-boot cold-artifact A/A characterization and the 0.8-1.2s figure was TUI navigation (worker-spawn-bound) - different surfaces from this lane's headless spawn path. decision: awaiting orchestrator: (1) spawn->first-response is NOT at floor - admission (per-child supervisor create) dominates at p50 264-342ms across all four regimes, and is NOT owned by #2857's mechanism; (2) the child kernel boot (probe+dill+python+import, 140-180ms) lands on the child's FIRST TOOL CALL (depth-0 prewarm gate) - kernel-boot's on-disk memo candidate owns that leg; prewarming children at create would add ~140-180ms to admission to remove it from the first tool call (net ~zero for the spawn->answer path), so the depth-gate tradeoff is NOT an obvious win and needs the operator ruling before any edit; (3) no edit proposed by this lane (baseline only, per the no-claim bar); (4) the parent-session-size effect rides the frozen turn-boundary release (129ms at 10MiB vs 33ms small) - TS parity, not a candidate.
